domain: paper SUT domain (pde_numerical: SciPy shape-preserving interpolation)
cat: O<= (monotone / linear shape-preservation: monotone data must give a monotone interpolant; two points must give the linear chord)
fix_title: BUG: Fix `Akima1DInterpolator` by returning linear interpolant for `y.shape[0] == 2` (#22278)
sut: two strictly-increasing points x=[0,1], y=[0,2]; the unique shape-preserving (linear) interpolant is the chord y=2x
mr_used: O<= shape-preservation: a shape-preserving 1-D interpolant of monotone data must be monotone, and through exactly two points the unique shape-preserving (linear) interpolant is the straight line. Operationally for two increasing points: (a) I((x0+x1)/2) == (y0+y1)/2 (on the chord) and max|I - chord| == 0 on the interior; (b) the sampled sequence is non-decreasing and stays within [y0,y1]. Source = the exact linear chord; follow-up = Akima1DInterpolator(x,y) on the interior grid.
fired_type: NUMERIC / CRASH (flaky manifestation, stable FIRED verdict). Pre 1.15.2: with only 2 points the slope scratch array m=empty(x.size+3)=empty(5) is filled only at m[2:3]; the ghost-slope formulas m[1]=2*m[2]-m[3], m[0]=2*m[1]-m[2], m[-2]=2*m[-3]-m[-4] READ UNINITIALISED np.empty entries, so the breakpoint slope is garbage. Depending on the np.empty buffer the construction either (i) raises ValueError('`dydx` must contain only finite values.') from non-finite slopes, or (ii) succeeds but returns a non-linear interpolant, e.g. I(0.5)=1.25 vs the chord value 1.0 (off by 0.25). Either way the O<= linear/monotone shape-preservation relation is violated. NOT an overflow-boundary case -- the two inputs are tiny finite numbers.

pre_observed.verdict: FIRED (stable across all 6 repeats; manifestation flaky due to uninitialised np.empty buffer)
